_note: Claim adjustment group/reason codes are public X12 standards. Plain-language entries below were written for this project and simplified for consumers.

chunks.title: Group code CO — Contractual Obligation
chunks.text: CO means the provider agreed by contract to write this amount off. A CO adjustment is the provider's responsibility, and it should never appear as an amount the member owes. If a provider bills you for a CO amount, that is generally improper balance billing under their network contract.

chunks.title: Group code PR — Patient Responsibility
chunks.text: PR means the amount is the member's responsibility under the plan design, such as a deductible, copay, or coinsurance. PR amounts are legitimate member costs, but they should still match the plan's stated deductible, copay, and coinsurance rules.

chunks.title: Group code OA — Other Adjustment
chunks.text: OA is used when no other group code fits, most commonly OA-23, which reflects the impact of a prior payer's decision when you have more than one insurance plan coordinating benefits.

chunks.title: PR-1 — Deductible
chunks.text: PR-1 means this amount was applied to your deductible, the amount you pay each year before the plan starts sharing costs. It counts toward both your deductible and your out-of-pocket maximum.

chunks.title: PR-2 — Coinsurance
chunks.text: PR-2 means this amount is coinsurance, your percentage share of the allowed amount after the deductible is met. Your plan documents state the percentage the plan pays and the percentage you pay.

chunks.title: PR-3 — Copayment
chunks.text: PR-3 means this amount is a copay, a fixed dollar amount for a covered visit or service. Copays typically do not depend on the deductible.

chunks.title: CO-45 — Charge exceeds contracted rate
chunks.text: CO-45 means the provider billed more than the rate they agreed to with the plan. The difference is written off by the provider. Members do not owe CO-45 amounts for in-network care.

chunks.title: CO-97 — Bundled into another service
chunks.text: CO-97 means payment for this service is included in the payment for another service performed the same day, a practice called bundling. The provider cannot separately bill the member for a bundled service.

chunks.title: CO-29 — Filed too late (timely filing)
chunks.text: CO-29 means the provider submitted the claim after the plan's filing deadline. Because this is the provider's error, the write-off is the provider's responsibility, and the member is generally not liable for the amount.

chunks.title: CO-50 — Not deemed medically necessary
chunks.text: CO-50 means the plan decided the service was not medically necessary under its rules. These denials can be appealed, and the treating clinician's notes are often the key evidence.

chunks.title: CO-18 — Duplicate claim or service
chunks.text: CO-18 means the plan believes this exact service was already submitted or paid. If a service truly appears twice on your paperwork, request an itemized bill and ask the provider's billing office to correct it.

chunks.title: PR-204 — Service not covered by this plan
chunks.text: PR-204 means this service is not a covered benefit under your plan, so the full allowed amount is your responsibility. You have the right to appeal if you believe the service should be covered, starting with an internal appeal.

chunks.title: OA-23 — Prior payer adjudication
chunks.text: OA-23 reflects the impact of a payment or adjustment already made by another insurance plan that pays before this one. Your secondary plan considers what the first plan did before calculating what remains.

chunks.title: CO-16 — Claim lacks information
chunks.text: CO-16 means the claim is missing information the plan needs, and a remark code should say what is missing. This is usually fixable paperwork between the provider and the plan, not a true denial.

chunks.title: Remark N130 — Check your plan documents
chunks.text: Remark code N130 directs you to review your plan's benefit documents for the rules that apply to this service. It usually accompanies a coverage limitation rather than an error.
